title: Private installer: bootstrap initial admin role bindings + validate IdP/group mapping
creator: Vivek Kulkarni
description:
Private installs are at risk of locking themselves out as we move to deny-by-default RBAC v2. We need a deterministic, auditable bootstrap path that creates the initial admin role binding(s) on install, and validates the customer’s IdP group mapping workflow (SAML/OIDC -> groups -> Redwood subject) before enforcing RBAC v2.

This ticket covers changes to the redwood-private-installer (and associated Helm charts/manifests) to:
1) Bootstrap initial admin access (role bindings) safely.
2) Validate IdP configuration and group claims for the configured admin group(s).
3) Provide a recovery path that does not permanently weaken security (time-bound / break-glass compatible).

Outcomes must be consistent across air-gapped and connected environments and must not override existing customer bindings on upgrade.

Key stakeholders:
- Private deployments PM: Vivek Kulkarni
- Authn/Authz integration: Kaitlyn Nguyen
- Policy engine: Jordan Lee
- Security Eng: Marcus Lin
- IT/Identity: David Kim
- SecOps: Fiona McCarthy
- Private pilot lead: Colin O'Donnell
acceptance_criteria: New Private install prompts for (or supports config of) an initial admin principal (IdP group recommended) and creates corresponding role binding(s) at first boot.

Installer validates that IdP group claim is present and matches expected value(s) via a deterministic preflight (see test plan). If validation fails, RBAC v2 enforcement remains disabled and the UI/CLI shows actionable errors.
Bootstrap is idempotent: safe to rerun without duplicating bindings or changing unrelated bindings.
Upgrades DO NOT overwrite customer-managed roles/role bindings; bootstrap only runs when no admin binding exists (or under an explicit "--force-bootstrap" break-glass flag).
All bootstrap actions are audit logged with sufficient context (who/what/when/how, installer version, cluster ID).
Documented recovery path exists for cases where IdP is unavailable/misconfigured at install time, aligned with break-glass controls (time-bound, alerting hooks where possible).
Automated e2e test covers: successful bootstrap, failed bootstrap due to missing group claim, upgrade path, and rerun/idempotency.
implementation_notes:
Proposed approach (subject to Security sign-off):

A) Config surface
- Add installer flags and Helm values:
  - rbac.bootstrap.enabled (default true for new installs)
  - rbac.bootstrap.initialAdminGroup (string, recommended)
  - rbac.bootstrap.initialAdminEmail (string, optional fallback for non-group IdPs)
  - rbac.bootstrap.roleTemplate (default "private:org-admin" or "private:security-admin" per policy bundle)
  - rbac.bootstrap.force (default false)

B) Bootstrap mechanism
- On first control-plane startup, a small bootstrap job (K8s Job or init container) calls a privileged internal endpoint to create role binding(s) if and only if:
  - No existing binding grants the required "rbac.*" + "org.*" admin permissions in the org scope, OR
  - rbac.bootstrap.force is true.
- The job should run with a tightly-scoped service account that can only call the bootstrap endpoint; it should not be a general cluster-admin.

C) Validation of IdP/group mapping
- Add an installer "preflight" step that can be invoked both interactively and via CI:
  - Requests a one-time login to the Console (or direct OIDC auth flow) and inspects the resulting ID token claims.
  - Verifies expected group claim key/value (configurable claim name; defaults: "groups").
  - Verifies that at least one configured admin group is present.
- If validation fails, do NOT turn on RBAC v2 enforcement flag in the deployment values, and provide an explicit error with remediation:
  - "Your IdP token did not include the groups claim. Ensure group claims are configured in your IdP app and that the user is a member of the admin group(s)."

D) Enforcement sequencing
- Ensure the rollout order does not brick installs:
  1) Install with RBAC v2 evaluation available but enforcement off.
  2) Bootstrap admin binding.
  3) Validate IdP group mapping.
  4) Enable enforcement flag.

E) Recovery / break-glass alignment
- Provide a documented break-glass path for initial setup only:
  - Option 1: time-bound local admin user (single-use) generated at install time and displayed once, stored as a hashed secret; expires after N hours.
  - Option 2: an explicit installer command that creates a temporary role binding for a provided subject, tagged and set to expire (requires control plane support).
- At minimum, add a prominent warning and require an explicit acknowledgement in CLI if using force/bootstrap override.

Open questions (need alignment):
- Should the initial role template be "Org Admin" or "Security Admin" for Private? (Leaning Security Admin + separate Billing/Operator templates per enterprise feedback.)
- Where should the bootstrap job run: installer phase vs in-cluster job at first boot? (In-cluster preferred for idempotency and upgrades.)
- Do we require customers to use group mapping, or support email-subject bootstrap as first-class? (Support both; group recommended.)
test_plan:
Automated:
- Add e2e suite in private installer CI using kind:
  1) Fresh install with bootstrap.initialAdminGroup set -> verify role binding exists; verify Console login for a user in group succeeds and can manage roles.
  2) Fresh install with bootstrap.initialAdminGroup set but IdP token lacks groups claim -> verify installer preflight fails and enforcement stays off; verify clear error output.
  3) Re-run install/upgrade -> verify bootstrap does not modify existing role bindings.
  4) Force bootstrap flag -> verify creates binding only when explicitly requested and emits audit log event.

Manual (pilot readiness):
- Validate with a real IdP (Okta + Azure AD) using documented app settings for group claims.
- Run through first-login experience with Colin’s pilot environment and confirm "why denied" guidance is not triggered for the intended admin user.

Security:
- Threat model review with Marcus Lin:
  - Ensure bootstrap credentials are not long-lived.
  - Ensure no plaintext secrets logged.
  - Ensure audit log includes bootstrap metadata for evidence.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (dogfood):
- Enable in internal Private staging clusters only.
- Monitor authz denials, installer failures, and supportability of error messages.

Phase 2 (pilot customers):
- Turn on for 1–2 Private POCs (Colin to coordinate) behind a feature flag in installer config.
- Require explicit sign-off from Security Eng before enabling enforcement by default.

Phase 3 (GA):
- Make bootstrap enabled by default for new installs; keep upgrade path non-invasive.
- Publish docs + runbook and add a support checklist for common IdP misconfigurations.
comments: 2025-02-12 — Vivek Kulkarni (PM): Marking P0 for Private POCs. We had a customer ask explicitly: “How do we guarantee we won’t lock ourselves out on day 0?” This needs to be part of the installer story, not a manual post-install runbook.

2025-02-14 — David Kim (IT/Identity): For IdP validation, please don’t assume group claims are always called "groups". Okta customers often use "groups", but Azure AD can be "groups" with IDs or a custom claim. We should let them configure claim name and match semantics (exact string, or regex prefix).

2025-02-18 — Marcus Lin (Security Eng): +1 bootstrap, but avoid any permanent local admin account as a default. If we need recovery, it must be time-bound, auditable, and ideally alerting-integrated. Force bootstrap should be noisy and should leave a strong audit trail.

2025-02-21 — Kaitlyn Nguyen (Assignee): Drafted implementation plan: in-cluster Job that calls internal control plane bootstrap endpoint. Working with Jordan on a minimal bootstrap API that only accepts “create binding if none exists” and supports TTL for temp binding. Will post API shape for review.

2025-02-26 — Jordan Lee (Policy engine): For the “admin exists” check, recommend evaluating for a permission set rather than role name. Role templates can drift; permission-based check prevents false negatives when templates change. Proposed check: subject has {rbac.roles.write, rbac.bindings.write, org.users.write} at org scope.

2025-03-02 — Fiona McCarthy (SecOps): If we introduce any break-glass mechanism, we need an alert trigger. At minimum: emit an audit event type "rbac.bootstrap" and "rbac.break_glass" that our SIEM export can key off. Also, ensure we can route to PagerDuty for pilot accounts.

2025-03-06 — Kaitlyn Nguyen (Assignee): Implemented Helm values + Job wiring in branch; still pending: preflight claim validation UX (installer CLI). Current thinking: add `installer preflight idp` command that prints detected claim keys and the matched groups. Need Design review for error text and next-step links.

2025-03-08 — Connor O'Brien (Release): Please ensure upgrade behavior is explicit. We can’t have a patch release that modifies existing role bindings. Add a guard + a release note callout. Also, we’ll likely need a backport to the current Private stable branch if pilots start before the next full release.
current_status_summary: In implementation. Helm/config + bootstrap Job wiring mostly complete; aligning on IdP preflight validation behavior and break-glass/recovery semantics. Security review scheduled with Marcus/Fiona before pilot enablement.
